30def _clone_kernel(src_ptr, dst_ptr, n_elements, BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr):

32 block_start = pid * BLOCK_SIZE 

33 offsets = block_start + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_SIZE) 

34 mask = offsets < n_elements 

35 vals = tl.load(src_ptr + offsets, mask=mask) 

36 tl.store(dst_ptr + offsets, vals, mask=mask)

67def _is_fake_or_meta(inp: torch.Tensor) -> bool: 

68 """Whether ``inp`` carries metadata only, with no storage to read or write. 

69 

70 ``aten::clone`` is a CompositeExplicitAutograd op whose Meta implementation 

71 is a "default backend kernel": shape propagation re-runs the backend 

72 implementation under the fake/meta mode instead of using a dedicated meta 

73 function. Because FlagGems takes over the device dispatch key, that 

74 fallback lands in this module, and the Triton launch below would ask a 

75 FakeTensor for ``data_ptr()`` -- which raises. Handle this case by 

76 deriving the output layout only. 

77 

78 ``FakeTensor`` is detected by its ``fake_mode`` attribute rather than by 

79 importing the class: it lives in a private module that has moved across 

80 torch releases, and a real meta tensor (``is_meta``) has no ``fake_mode``, 

81 so both spellings are covered without a version-sensitive import. A plain 

82 eager tensor on a real device has neither attribute and never takes this 

83 path.

96 # Tensors that live outside the accelerator (e.g. CPU tensors materialised by 

97 # a multimodal front-end) must never reach the Triton kernel: the device 

98 # guard inside ``_launch_copy`` rejects them on backends such as torch_gcu 

99 # ("Expected a gcu device, but got: cpu", FlagGems #8529). A native copy 

100 # keeps the requested memory format and dtype without touching the device. 

101 if inp.device.type != runtime.device.name: 

102 if memory_format == torch.preserve_format: 

103 out = _allocate_preserve_format(inp) 

104 else: 

105 out = torch.empty_like(inp, memory_format=memory_format) 

106 out.copy_(inp) 

107 return out 

108 

109 if inp.numel() == 0: 

110 if memory_format == torch.preserve_format: 

111 return _allocate_preserve_format(inp) 

112 return torch.empty_like(inp, memory_format=memory_format)

114 # Metadata-only inputs (FakeTensor under torch.compile/export, or a tensor 

115 # on the meta device) have no storage: every branch below would either 

116 # launch a Triton kernel or dispatch a copy that eventually reads a data 

117 # pointer. Resolve the layout here instead.

121 # Triton has no complex dtype mapping. Following the project convention 

122 # (see detach_copy, ravel, slice_copy, etc.), complex tensors are 

123 # reinterpreted through ``torch.view_as_real`` as interleaved (real, imag) 

124 # pairs so the existing Triton copy kernel operates on real-valued data. 

125 # ``view_as_real`` appends a trailing size-2 axis, preserving contiguity of 

126 # the original layout. For contiguous / non-overlapping-dense inputs the 

127 # flat Triton kernel can be used directly; non-contiguous or non-standard 

128 # memory-format requests fall back to ``Tensor.copy_`` which handles 

129 # arbitrary strides natively. 

130 if inp.is_complex(): 

131 # Resolve lazy conjugate/negative bits so view_as_real reads the 

132 # logical values (same pattern as detach_copy). 

133 if inp.is_conj(): 

134 inp = inp.resolve_conj() 

135 is_neg = getattr(inp, "is_neg", None) 

136 if is_neg is not None and is_neg():

153 # Tensor.copy_ handles the strided-to-contiguous copy natively. 

154 out.copy_(inp)
